Name: OneThing API
Description:
OneThing turns a photo, a link or a picked product into a live one-product shop that takes
PayPal payments, or a recommendation page that earns referral commissions through Channel3.

**How a shop is made**
1. `createShop`: start from a photo, a link, or a Channel3 product. Gemini guesses what it
   is, how it's delivered, the price, a short link and the page design. You get back the
   shop's link name and an **admin token**.
2. `updateShop`: correct anything the AI guessed, then set `status: live`.
3. Buyers pay on `https://<host>/<slug>` with PayPal. Sellers read orders and ship them.

**Auth.** Seller endpoints take the shop's admin token in the `x-admin-token` header, or a
**platform API key** (`Authorization: Bearer ot_sk_…`) for marketplaces that make shops for
their own sellers. Buyer endpoints (checkout, access-code verification, downloads) are public.

**Access codes.** A digital product can unlock an app or game instead of shipping a file.
Each paid order gets a code such as `K7QF-M2XP-9HTD`; your app calls `verifyAccessCode`
before unlocking. Raptor Rush on miriogames.com is a live example.

**Agent-ready.** Every live shop is also published for AI shopping agents: an MCP server at
`/api/mcp` with `search_shops`, `get_product`, `create_order` and `get_order`, and the same
four as plain GETs for assistants that can only fetch URLs (`listAgentShops`,
`getAgentProduct`, `orderByLink`, `getAgentOrder`), with `/llms.txt` as the starting point.
An agent can find and order, but the buyer still approves every payment at PayPal.

All money moves through PayPal (sandbox in this deployment). OneThing never holds card data.

Endpoints.Name: signIn
Endpoints.Description: Signs in with an email address or a phone number, creating the account the first time. There's no password and no verification (sandbox). The response sets the `ot_session` cookie; shops created with it belong to the account and are listed on `/account`. Signing in with an email also claims older shops whose seller email matches. In a browser, sellers can instead use Log in with PayPal (`/api/account/paypal`), which also records the PayPal account their sales are paid into.

Endpoints.Name: createShop
Endpoints.Description:
Starts a draft shop from one of three sources. Gemini designs the page and guesses the
setup; check it with `getShop`, adjust with `updateShop`, then go live.

Sent with a session cookie from `signIn`, the shop belongs to that account, which also
becomes its seller email (and PayPal email, after Log in with PayPal) unless you give one.

- `source=photo`: a `photo` and/or a `description` of your own product.
- `source=link`: a `url`. If Channel3 recognises it as a store's product page, the shop
  becomes a recommendation (`product_type: referral`); otherwise the page is read and you
  sell the product yourself with PayPal.
- `source=channel3`: a `productId` from `searchProducts` (a recommendation).

Takes 15–40 seconds. Hero art, if available, is generated afterwards (`hero_status`).

**Platforms:** sent with a platform API key, the shop belongs to the key's account, so the
key can manage it from then on (no need to keep the admin token). It's made for one of the
platform's sellers, so it inherits nothing from the account: set `paypal_email` or call
`connectPayPal` for that seller.

listing doesn't say (dimensions, materials). `createShop` already does this once; call it

Endpoints.Name: connectPayPal
Endpoints.Description:
Starts PayPal's seller onboarding (Partner Referrals). Send the seller's browser to the
returned `url`; they sign in to PayPal (or create a business account) and grant OneThing
permission. PayPal brings them back to `/api/shops/<slug>/paypal/return`, which saves the
connection and opens the manage page. From then on, sales are paid to that account.

Without a connection, a shop can still go live with a typed `paypal_email`.

**Platforms:** call it with your API key and a `returnUrl`, and PayPal's flow ends on your own
page instead, as `returnUrl?paypal=connected|incomplete|cancelled|failed&shop=<slug>`. The
URL's origin must be one registered on the key.

Endpoints.Name: orderByLink
Endpoints.Description:
Orders one unit with a GET: the MCP `create_order` tool for AI assistants that can only
fetch URLs, such as free-tier ChatGPT or Grok. Nothing is charged. The reply has `pay_url`,
where the buyer pays at PayPal, and `status_url` (`getAgentOrder`), which says when they
have and what they got.

For a product with options, pass the buyer's pick as query parameters named after the
options (`?Size=9`, or `?Color=Ice+Blue&Size=L`); names and values are matched without
regard to case. You rarely build this URL yourself: `getAgentProduct` and `/llms.txt`
write it out in full (`order_url`, or `variants[].order_url`), because some assistants
only open URLs they have been shown.

Every request makes a new order, so open it once, after the buyer says to buy. A link
previewer opening it leaves an unpaid order at most: stock is only taken when a payment
is captured. Replies are `no-store` and `X-Robots-Tag: noindex, nofollow`.

Endpoints.Name: callMcp
Endpoints.Description:
A [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) server, so agents such as
Claude can shop here. Add `https://<host>/api/mcp` to an MCP client as a Streamable HTTP
server. It's stateless: each POST carries one JSON-RPC 2.0 message (or a batch) and gets a
plain JSON reply, with no event stream. The `initialize` reply's `Mcp-Session-Id` header
carries the client's `clientInfo.name`; send it back on later requests (MCP clients do)
so the seller's stats show which agent sent the buyer. Nothing else is kept.

Methods: `initialize`, `ping`, `tools/list`, `tools/call`. Tools:

| Tool | Arguments | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `search_shops` | `query?`, `limit?` (1–25) | Live gallery shops whose name or headline has every word |
| `get_product` | `shop` | The same object as `getAgentProduct` |
| `create_order` | `shop`, `options?` | One unit on order; returns `order_id` and `pay_url` |
| `get_order` | `order_id` | Status and `next_step`; once paid, the receipt and `delivery` |

**The buyer always approves.** `create_order` charges nothing: the agent shows the buyer
`pay_url` (`/o/<order_id>`, see `openPayLink`), which opens PayPal. It's a plain link on this
site, so agent platforms that hide PayPal's checkout tokens can still show it. When the buyer
says they've paid, the agent calls `get_order`.

`get_order` status is one of `awaiting_buyer_approval`, `paid`, `declined` (nothing charged;
the buyer can open `pay_url` again), `sold_out`, `expired` (call `create_order` again) or
`failed` (PayPal couldn't be reached; try again), with a `next_step` the agent can follow.
A paid order carries `delivery`: `{type: access_code, access_code, start_url?}`,
`{type: download, download_url}` or `{type: shipping, ship_to, fulfillment, tracking}`, plus
`amount` with item, shipping and total. Orders made this way show `channel: agent` in
`listOrders`.

Tool errors (an unknown shop, a sold-out size) come back as results with `isError: true`,
so the model can read them and try something else.
Endpoints.Summary: MCP server for AI shopping agents
